subject: Control plane / keystore escrow — evidence request and operator-access boundaries
messages:
From: Danielle Moore <d.moore@acmepharm.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmepharm.com>; Tom Riley <t.riley@acmepharm.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Control plane and keystore escrow — evidence and operator access

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Legal asked me to follow up with a concrete list of the evidence and guarantees we need to close the DPA annex for our private deployment. Our key concerns are:

- Confirmation that the control plane cannot access tenant plaintext model inputs/outputs when BYOK is enabled.
- Exact subprocessors (operators/on-call) that will have the ability to perform maintenance on the private deployment, and the conditions under which that access is allowed.
- Escrow process for CMKs: what artifacts are stored, who can request release, and geo limitations for escrowed material.
- Proof we can provide to our auditors for SOC2-like controls (redacted logs, telemetry schema, red team results).

Can you send a short checklist and any sample evidence docs we can show to our InfoSec team? Also need an outline of the operational runbook (breakglass procedure + SLA windows) that your ops team would follow if we request emergency key recovery.

Appreciate it — Danielle

--
Danielle Moore
Head of IT Risk, Acme Pharmaceuticals

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Moore <d.moore@acmepharm.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control plane and keystore escrow — evidence request and operator-access boundaries

Danielle —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve looped in Kimberly (Security & Compliance) and Priyom (Infra) to provide the technical artifacts and runbook excerpts. High-level answers up front:

- With BYOK enabled in a private VPC deployment, customer CMKs are used for envelope encryption of data at rest and for sealing the runtime; the Redwood control plane has no standing ability to decrypt tenant payloads.
- Operator access is limited to ephemeral, auditable maintenance sessions and only when pre-authorized via the mutual action plan. We can enumerate by role and provide an access matrix.
- Escrow: we offer an optional CMK-escrow process scoped to recovery-only (not automated rekeying). Escrow artifacts are encrypted under a multi-party envelope and only released on signed request + customer ACL approvals.

I’ll attach a one-page checklist and propose a short follow-up meeting to walk through the evidence pack. Priyom/Kim, can you attach the SOC2 snapshot, the operator-access matrix, and a short excerpt of the escrow procedure?

Next steps I propose here:
1) Review the attached checklist (I included a proposed mutual action plan).
2) Internal review by Acme InfoSec and list any additional evidence items by 2027-11-11.
3) 30-min working session (Nov 12) to go over the runbook and sign the annex.

Thanks,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 08:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control plane and keystore escrow — evidence request and operator-access boundaries

Folks — attaching the artifacts per Sergio's ask: SOC2 snapshot (redacted), operator-access matrix, and a short excerpt from our BYOK/escrow procedure. Summary of key assurances (short bullets for Acme Legal):

- Data access boundaries: With BYOK + private VPC, runtime keys are derived inside customer-controlled HSMs (or your KMS) and envelope keys never transit readable to Redwood control plane. We log and redact all control-plane telemetry to avoid exfil of PII or model content.
- Operator roles: enumerated in operator-access-matrix.xlsx — roles: On-call Technician, Infrastructure Engineer, Security Auditor. Access is time-bounded, ticketed, recorded (session recording and syslog) and requires at least two approvals from customer's delegated approvers for breakglass.
- Escrow mechanics: escrow artifacts are a wrapped key package plus audit metadata and are stored encrypted in an air-gapped escrow store. Release requires: (a) signed DocuSign release from customer's admin, (b) 2FA of Redwood escrow custodian, (c) cross-check against M-Action Plan state.
- Geo controls: escrow storage regions can be constrained to US-only or EU-only; we will commit region in annex.
- Evidence: we can provide redacted session logs, signed hash manifests of escrow packages, and a SOC2 snapshot. We cannot share full unredacted tenant data; we can provide schema and sample redacted excerpts.

Attachments: soc2-snapshot-2027Q3.pdf; operator-access-matrix.xlsx; redwood-byok-escrow-procedure.pdf

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Moore <d.moore@acmepharm.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmepharm.com>; Tom Riley <t.riley@acmepharm.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control plane and keystore escrow — evidence request and operator-access boundaries

Sergio / Kimberly —

This is helpful, thank you. A couple of clarifying asks from our auditors:

1) For the session recordings and syslog — can you provide a sample redacted session with the exact fields that will be present? (we don’t need a live one; a 1–2 page redacted sample is fine).
2) Can you confirm the maximum retention window for operator session recordings and the ability for Acme to request deletion/archival?
3) For escrow release, we need to confirm an SLA on turnaround time (we assume two business days + verification). Can Redwood commit to an SLA or do you require a different timeline?

Also — we prefer escrow storage to be US-only. Please note that in the annex draft.

If possible, can we do the 30-min working session on Nov 12 at 10:30am PT? That would help flatten open items.

Best,
Danielle

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Moore <d.moore@acmepharm.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>; Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2027 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control plane and keystore escrow — evidence request and operator-access boundaries

Danielle —

Thanks — confirmed Nov 12, 10:30am PT on my calendar (meeting invite sent). Quick answers inline:

1) Sample redacted session: yes — we will provide a two-page redacted session extract that shows timestamps, user principals, commands executed, and hashes of objects accessed (no tenant data). See linked Drive doc: https://redwood.app/drive/mnap-acme-20271110 (I uploaded the sample session and the M-Action Plan).
2) Retention windows: default retention for operator-session recordings is 90 days; can be reduced or extended in the annex. We will include an SLA-backed deletion/archival request path (customer-initiated retention policy changes take effect within 5 business days).
3) Escrow SLA: Redwood proposes a 2 business-day SLA for initial verification and release of escrow packages once the signed request and customer approvals are validated. We will codify the release checklist in the annex; exceptional legal holds will pause release until cleared.

Kimberly/Priyom — please prepare the redacted session extract and the updated annex language for US-only escrow storage ahead of the session. I attached the mutual action plan (mnap-acme-20271110.xlsx) with proposed milestones.

Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mnap-acme-20271110.xlsx
